text:
maria_support: Hey team — customer acme-pay reporting intermittent TLS handshake failures when calling their service endpoint (svc.acme-pay.internal). Happens only from their prod VPC, started after they attached a new private hosted zone.

devon_network: Can you paste the exact error from the client logs? TLS? SNI?

maria_support: Error from app logs: "tls: certificate is not valid for any names, certificate=CN=svc.internal.example.com, subjectAltName=[svc.internal.example.com]". Client expects svc.acme-pay.internal.

sam_sre: That screams split-horizon. If Route53 private hosted zone has a record that resolves svc.acme-pay.internal -> CNAME -> svc.internal.example.com (internal cert), client SNI mismatch. Can you run dig from a host in the prod VPC?

maria_support: Ran dig from an ec2 in prod: `dig +short svc.acme-pay.internal` -> `svc.internal.example.com.`

maria_support: Also did `curl -v https://svc.acme-pay.internal/health` -> shows `* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello` then `* SSL: certificate subject name 'svc.internal.example.com' does not match target host 'svc.acme-pay.internal'` and curl exits with 51.

devon_network: Do we have the customer's Route53 hosted-zone associations? route53-bot: `aws route53 list-hosted-zones` + `list-vpc-association-authorizations` might help.

maria_support: customer confirms they created a private hosted zone acme-pay.internal and associated it with prod VPC, but a preexisting team-owned private zone internal.example.com has a CNAME from svc.acme-pay.internal -> svc.internal.example.com as part of internal service routing.

jen_prodeng: If the private hosted zone acme-pay.internal exists in the same VPC, its records should win for that name. But Route53 chooses the hosted zone with the longest matching name; however identical names conflict. Can you `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name acme-pay.internal` and `get-hosted-zone` to see record sets?

maria_support: Output: hosted zone acme-pay.internal has no A/CNAME for svc.acme-pay.internal (they only added a zone and a couple of top-level SRV records), so resolver falls through to the other private zone which has the CNAME.

sam_sre: Ok that explains DNS. Next are mitigation options: 1) customer adds an explicit A/ALIAS record in their acme-pay.internal hosted zone that points to the correct load balancer (preferred) 2) remove the conflicting record from internal.example.com if appropriate 3) use VPC resolver rule to forward or block.

devon_network: Also check node-local caches on their EKS nodes — I saw cases where stale node-local cache returned old answers after hosted zone changes. Run `kubectl exec -n kube-system $(kubectl get pods -l k8s-app=node-local-dns -o name) -- getent hosts svc.acme-pay.internal` and flush if needed.

maria_support: Customer tried restarting node-local-dns and the curl started returning the correct cert for a few minutes, then flipped back to the wrong cert.

jen_prodeng: That flip suggests DNS is inconsistent across AZs or resolver rules differ per subnet. Check resolver rule associations: `aws route53resolver list-resolver-rule-associations --filters Name=VPC,Values=vpc-xxxxx` and ensure only the intended rules apply.

maria_support: They ran that, found an orphaned resolver rule in a different AWS account that forwards acme-pay.internal to an internal resolver which still serves the old CNAME. Orphan rule association -> cross-account resolver rule was accidentally shared.

sam_sre: Great catch. Short-term fix: remove the cross-account rule association for that VPC (or update the forwarding target) so queries go to the local Route53 private zone. Long-term: customer should create explicit A/ALIAS in their acme-pay.internal hosted zone and rotate cert to include both names if multi-zone resolution needed.

devon_network: Also advise them to add the correct FQDN to the TLS cert (subjectAltName includes svc.acme-pay.internal).

maria_support: I pushed the immediate remediation steps to the customer: remove resolver association + add explicit A record. Asking them to confirm after changes.

jen_prodeng: One more thing — if they have egress allowlists or firewall appliances doing DNS intercept (ingress/egress proxies), make sure those do not rewrite or cache the wrong answer.

maria_support: Customer confirms removing resolver association fixed resolution across all nodes and TLS errors went away. Marking as resolved, will follow up on adding authoritative records and cert updates. :white_check_mark:

sam_sre: Nice. Closing notes for KB: include commands we used, the common symptom (SNI mismatch + CNAME to internal host), tracer commands, and the cross-account resolver rule gotcha.

maria_support: Will draft KB and link here. Thanks all! :tada:
